claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Pham et al., 2018 and Steggerda et al., 2017, which describe CB-1158's activity against human arginase.

claims.claim: CB-1158 is being tested in a phase I clinical trial in patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumors
claims.source: CB-1158 also inhibits human arginase, and it is being tested in a phase I clinical trial in patients with advanced or metastatic solid tumors (Pham et al., 2018; Steggerda et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Pham et al., 2018 and Steggerda et al., 2017, which describe the clinical testing of CB-1158.

claims.claim: A dual-recombinase approach was used to delete Arg1 in myeloid cell lineages via Cre-loxP technology while inducing oncogenic Kras in pancreatic epithelial cells using Flp-Frt recombination
claims.source: Here, we used a dual-recombinase approach to delete Arg1 in myeloid cell lineages via Cre-loxP technology and at the same time induced oncogenic Kras in pancreatic epithelial cells using the orthogonal Flp-Frt recombination approach.
claims.evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claims.claim: Arg1 deletion in myeloid cells profoundly reshaped the TME, increased the infiltration of CD8+ T cells, and reduced malignant disease progression
claims.source: We discovered that Arg1 deletion in myeloid cells profoundly reshaped the TME, increased the infiltration of CD8+ T cells, and reduced malignant disease progression.
claims.evidence: This represents a summary of the experimental findings from the genetic model described in the study.

claims.claim: Other cells in the TME, such as epithelial cells, upregulate Arg1 expression as a resistance mechanism when Arg1 is inactivated in myeloid cells
claims.source: However, we also noticed a resistance mechanism whereby other cells in the TME, such as epithelial cells, upregulate Arg1 expression, potentially blunting the effect of its inactivation in myeloid cells.
claims.evidence: This represents an observation from the experimental data showing compensatory Arg1 expression.

claims.claim: Treatment of a syngeneic orthotopic model of pancreatic cancer with CB-1158 sensitized tumors to anti-PD1 immune checkpoint blockade
claims.source: We thus employed a systemic approach, whereby we treated a syngeneic orthotopic model of pancreatic cancer with the arginase inhibitor CB-1158 and found it to sensitize PDA to anti-PD1 immune checkpoint blockade.
claims.evidence: This represents a key finding from the pharmacological experiments in the study.

claims.claim: ARG1 expression in CD45+ cells was prevalent in human PDA
claims.source: We observed prevalent ARG1 expression in CD45+ cells, and occasional low expression in ECAD+ cells (Figure 1A, Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RNA in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1A and quantified in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: ARG1 expression in ECAD+ cells was occasional and low in human PDA
claims.source: We observed prevalent ARG1 expression in CD45+ cells, and occasional low expression in ECAD+ cells (Figure 1A, Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by RNA in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1A and quantified in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: Analysis of sc-RNA-seq dataset from 16 human PDA samples revealed highest expression of ARG1 in myeloid cells
claims.source: Analysis of a previously published sc-RNA-seq dataset, which includes 16 human PDA samples (Steele et al., 2020; Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), revealed highest expression of ARG1 in myeloid cells (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of published sc-RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: Minimal ARG1 expression was observed in CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, epithelial cells, and fibroblasts in human PDA
claims.source: In contrast, we observed minimal ARG1 expression in CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, epithelial cells, and fibroblasts (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sc-RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: ARG2 was expressed at high levels in endocrine cells in human PDA
claims.source: ARG2 was expressed at high levels in endocrine cells, and at lower, but detectable levels in epithelial cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sc-RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: ARG2 was expressed at lower, but detectable levels in epithelial cells in human PDA
claims.source: ARG2 was expressed at high levels in endocrine cells, and at lower, but detectable levels in epithelial cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sc-RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Myeloid cells are the main source of ARG1 in the pancreatic cancer microenvironment
claims.source: Thus, we conclude that myeloid cells are the main source of ARG1 in the pancreatic cancer microenvironment.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the RNA ISH and sc-RNA-seq data presented in Figure 1.

claims.claim: Infiltration of myeloid cells, specifically macrophages, in pancreatic cancer portends worse patient survival
claims.source: Infiltration of myeloid cells, specifically macrophages, in pancreatic cancer portends worse patient survival (Sanford et al., 2013; Tsujikawa et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Sanford et al., 2013 and Tsujikawa et al., 2017.

claims.claim: High ARG1 expression in pancreatic cancer correlated with worse survival
claims.source: Based on a publicly available human PDA microarray data set (GSE71729) (Moffitt et al., 2015), we found that high ARG1 expression in pancreatic cancer correlated with worse survival (Figure 1E)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by survival analysis of the GSE71729 dataset shown in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: High ARG1 expression correlating with worse survival suggests that ARG1 in myeloid cells may play a functional role in human PDA
claims.source: we found that high ARG1 expression in pancreatic cancer correlated with worse survival (Figure 1E), suggesting that ARG1 in myeloid cells may play a functional role in human PDA.
claims.evidence: This represents an inference based on the survival analysis data.

claims.claim: The highest level of Arg1 expression in mouse pancreatic cancer was detected in macrophages
claims.source: We detected the highest level of Arg1 expression in macrophages (Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sc-RNA-seq data from mouse models shown in Figure 1G.

claims.claim: Arg1 expression was enriched in PDA infiltrating macrophages compared to macrophages in the normal pancreas
claims.source: Importantly, Arg1 expression was enriched in PDA infiltrating macrophages compared to macrophages in the normal pancreas (Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sc-RNA-seq data comparing healthy and PDA mouse tissue shown in Figure 1G.

claims.claim: Epithelial cells and fibroblasts only had sporadic Arg1 expression in mouse pancreatic cancer
claims.source: Other cell types, such as epithelial cells and fibroblasts, only had sporadic Arg1 expression.
claims.evidence: This is based on the sc-RNA-seq analysis of mouse pancreatic cancer.

claims.claim: Arg2 was expressed in macrophages at low levels in mouse pancreatic cancer
claims.source: Arg2 was also expressed in macrophages, albeit at low levels, and was the prevalent isoform in tumor-associated granulocytes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sc-RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: Arg2 was the prevalent isoform in tumor-associated granulocytes in mouse pancreatic cancer
claims.source: Arg2 was also expressed in macrophages, albeit at low levels, and was the prevalent isoform in tumor-associated granulocytes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sc-RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: ARG1 protein was not detected in the healthy pancreas
claims.source: We did not detect ARG1 protein in the healthy pancreas.
claims.evidence: This is based on co-immunofluorescence staining experiments.

claims.claim: Both PanIN and PDA presented with frequent co-localization of the macrophage marker F4/80 with ARG1
claims.source: In contrast, both PanIN and PDA presented with frequent co-localization of the macrophage marker F4/80 with ARG1, consistent with prevalent expression in this cell population (Figure 1H and I and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 1H and quantified in Figure 1I.

claims.claim: Expression of ARG1 in cell types other than macrophages was rare in mouse pancreatic lesions
claims.source: Consistent with human data, expression of ARG1 in other cell types was rare (Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1H.

claims.claim: In both mouse and human pancreatic cancer, ARG1 is highly expressed and largely confined to tumors, where it is predominantly expressed in macrophages
claims.source: Thus, both in mouse and human pancreatic cancer, ARG1 is highly expressed and largely confined to tumors, where it is predominantly expressed in macrophages.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the combined data from human and mouse samples presented in Figure 1.

claims.claim: Lyz2Cre/+;Arg1f/f TAMs had none or very low ARG1 protein, indicating efficient Cre recombination
claims.source: ARG1 expression was readily detectable in WT TAMs; in contrast, Lyz2Cre/+;Arg1f/f TAMs had none or very low ARG1 protein, indicating efficient Cre recombination (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Elevated levels of L-Arginine were observed in the Lyz2Cre/+;Arg1f/f TAM medium compared with WT TAM medium
claims.source: We thus performed extracellular metabolomics by liquid chromatography couple tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) and observed elevated levels of L-Arginine in the Lyz2Cre/+;Arg1f/f TAM medium compared with WT TAM medium (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: WT TAMs deplete arginine from their growth medium at an enhanced rate, relative to TAMs lacking Arg1 expression
claims.source: This finding is consistent with WT TAMs depleting arginine from their growth medium at an enhanced rate, relative to TAMs lacking Arg1 expression.
claims.evidence: This represents an inference based on the metabolomics data showing elevated arginine in Arg1-deficient TAM media.

claims.claim: 16 out of 26 KF mice (62%) had invasive disease at 9-16 months of age
claims.source: Accordingly, 16 out of 26 KF mice (62%) had invasive disease; in contrast, only 5 out of 24 KFCA mice had progressed (21%) (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by histopathological evaluation data shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: Only 5 out of 24 KFCA mice (21%) had invasive disease at 9-16 months of age
claims.source: Accordingly, 16 out of 26 KF mice (62%) had invasive disease; in contrast, only 5 out of 24 KFCA mice had progressed (21%) (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by histopathological evaluation data shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: High ARG1 expression was observed in macrophages in KF tissues
claims.source: As expected, we observed high ARG1 expression in macrophages in KF tissues and little to no ARG1 expression in macrophages in KFCA pancreata (Figure 2F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: Little to no ARG1 expression was observed in macrophages in KFCA pancreata
claims.source: As expected, we observed high ARG1 expression in macrophages in KF tissues and little to no ARG1 expression in macrophages in KFCA pancreata (Figure 2F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: Substantial ARG1 expression was observed in epithelial cells from the KFCA pancreata
claims.source: Surprisingly, we observed substantial ARG1 expression in epithelial cells from the KFCA pancreata, while epithelial cells in KF mice had little to no ARG1 expression (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: Epithelial cells in KF mice had little to no ARG1 expression
claims.source: Surprisingly, we observed substantial ARG1 expression in epithelial cells from the KFCA pancreata, while epithelial cells in KF mice had little to no ARG1 expression (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: Deletion of Arg1 in myeloid cells impairs malignant progression but unleashes a compensatory upregulation of Arg1 in epithelial cells
claims.source: So, while deletion of Arg1 in myeloid cells impairs malignant progression, it unleashes a compensatory upregulation of Arg1 in epithelial cells.
claims.evidence: This represents a conclusion based on the histopathology and immunofluorescence data.

claims.claim: The epithelia that expressed ARG1 in KFCA mice had an elongated appearance, consistent with tuft cells
claims.source: We noted that the epithelia that expressed ARG1 in KFCA mice had an elongated appearance, consistent with tuft cells, a cell type that is not present in the healthy pancreas but common in low-grade PanINs (Delgiorno et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on morphological observations and is supported by citation to Delgiorno et al., 2014 about tuft cells.

claims.claim: Tuft cells are not present in the healthy pancreas but are common in low-grade PanINs
claims.source: We noted that the epithelia that expressed ARG1 in KFCA mice had an elongated appearance, consistent with tuft cells, a cell type that is not present in the healthy pancreas but common in low-grade PanINs (Delgiorno et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Delgiorno et al., 2014.

claims.claim: Tuft cells are the exclusive source of epithelial ARG1 in KFCA samples
claims.source: By co-immunostaining for the tuft cell marker COX1, we confirmed that tuft cells are the exclusive source of epithelial ARG1 in these samples (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: Tuft cell ARG1 expression suggests a tuft cell response to accumulating arginine in the microenvironment
claims.source: By co-immunostaining for the tuft cell marker COX1, we confirmed that tuft cells are the exclusive source of epithelial ARG1 in these samples (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A), suggesting a tuft cell response to accumulating arginine in the microenvironment.
claims.evidence: This represents an inference about the biological significance of tuft cell ARG1 expression.

claims.claim: The percentage of total macrophages was similar between KF and KFCA pancreas
claims.source: The percentage of total macrophages was similar between KF and KFCA pancreas (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sc-RNA-seq and immunohistochemistry data shown in the supplementary figures.

claims.claim: Five different macrophage populations were identified based on distinct gene profiles in KF and KFCA pancreata
claims.source: We then subclustered the macrophages, from which we identified five different macrophage populations based on distinct gene profiles (Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sc-RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 2H.

claims.claim: The macrophage 1 population was defined by Apoe, C1qa, and C1qc markers of TAMs in mouse and human pancreatic cancer
claims.source: The macrophage 1 population was defined by Apoe, C1qa, and C1qc markers of TAMs in mouse and human pancreatic cancer (Kemp et al., 2021a)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sc-RNA-seq data and citation to Kemp et al., 2021a.

claims.claim: The macrophage 5 population expressed Ear2 and Retnla
claims.source: while the macrophage 5 population expressed Ear2 and Retnla (Figure 2H).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sc-RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2H.

claims.claim: Macrophage APOE is tumor promoting
claims.source: Since macrophage APOE (Apolipoprotein E) is tumor promoting (Kemp et al., 2021a)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Kemp et al., 2021a.

claims.claim: A reduction in APOE expression was detected in KFCA compared to KF
claims.source: we performed co-immunofluorescent staining for APOE, F4/80, and ECAD and detected a reduction in APOE expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 3D and E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3D and quantified in 3E.

claims.claim: Deletion of Arg1 in myeloid cells led to an upregulation of Arg2 expression, mainly in the macrophage 4 population
claims.source: Intriguingly, sc-RNA-seq revealed that deletion of Arg1 in myeloid cells led to an upregulation of Arg2 expression, mainly in the macrophage 4 population expressing Chil3, Ly6c2, and Clec4e genes (Figure 2I)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sc-RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2I.

claims.claim: The upregulation of Arg2 in KFCA macrophages suggests the existence of a compensatory mechanism
claims.source: Intriguingly, sc-RNA-seq revealed that deletion of Arg1 in myeloid cells led to an upregulation of Arg2 expression, mainly in the macrophage 4 population expressing Chil3, Ly6c2, and Clec4e genes (Figure 2I), suggesting the existence of a compensatory mechanism.
claims.evidence: This represents an inference based on the Arg2 upregulation observed in the sc-RNA-seq data.

claims.claim: KFCA macrophages exhibited upregulation of signaling pathways involved in MHC I antigen processing and cross presentation
claims.source: Interestingly, KFCA macrophages, mainly the macrophage 3 population, exhibited upregulation of signaling pathways involved in MHC I antigen processing and cross presentation (Figure 2J and Figure 2—figure supplement 3H)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by reactome pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2J.

claims.claim: Upregulation of MHC I antigen processing pathways in KFCA macrophages suggests an improvement in antigen-specific CD8+ T cell activation upon Arg1 deletion
claims.source: Interestingly, KFCA macrophages, mainly the macrophage 3 population, exhibited upregulation of signaling pathways involved in MHC I antigen processing and cross presentation (Figure 2J and Figure 2—figure supplement 3H), suggesting an improvement in antigen-specific CD8+ T cell activation upon Arg1 deletion.
claims.evidence: This represents an inference based on the pathway analysis data.

claims.claim: Increased CD8+ T cell infiltration was observed in KFCA pancreata compared to KF
claims.source: As sc-RNA-seq suggested that Arg1 null macrophages have higher antigen presenting activity, we stained KF and KFCA pancreata for CD8 and observed increased CD8+ T cell infiltration in the latter (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: An increase in the percentage of both cytotoxic and exhausted CD8+ T cells was observed in the KFCA model compared with KF
claims.source: From this analysis, we observed an increase in the percentage of both cytotoxic and exhausted CD8+ T cells in the KFCA model compared with KF (Figure 3D and E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sc-RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 3D and E.

claims.claim: Expression of genes related to CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity, including Gzmb, Prfn1, and Ifng was upregulated in CD8+ T cells from the KFCA model
claims.source: Correspondingly, expression of genes related to CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity, including Granzyme b (Gzmb), Perforin 1 (Prfn1), and Interferon gamma (Ifng) was upregulated in CD8+ T cells from the KFCA model (Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sc-RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3F.

claims.claim: An increase in GZMB-expressing CD8+ T cells was observed in KFCA pancreata
claims.source: Accordingly, co-immunofluorescent staining for CD8, GZMB, and ECAD showed an increase in GZMB-expressing CD8+ T cells in KFCA pancreata (Figure 3G and H).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3G and quantified in Figure 3H.

claims.claim: Expression of genes involved in T cell exhaustion such as Ctla4, Furin, Lag3, and Pdcd1 was upregulated in the KFCA model compared with the KF
claims.source: We also found that the expression of genes involved in T cell exhaustion such as cytotoxic T-lymphocyte associated protein 4 (Ctla4), Furin, lymphocyte activating 3 (Lag3), and programmed cell death 1 (Pdcd1) was upregulated in the KFCA model, compared with the KF (Figure 3I).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by sc-RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3I.

claims.claim: Deletion of Arg1 in myeloid cells resulted in an increase in CD8+ T cell infiltration and activation, counterbalanced by an increase in exhaustion
claims.source: Taken together, deletion of Arg1 in myeloid cells resulted in an increase in CD8+ T cell infiltration and activation, counterbalanced by an increase in exhaustion as well.
claims.evidence: This represents a summary conclusion based on the CD8+ T cell data presented in Figure 3.

claims.claim: Systemic inhibition of Arginase by CB-1158 increased the infiltration of CD8+ T cells in orthotopic pancreatic tumors
claims.source: Interestingly, we observed that systemic inhibition of Arginase by CB-1158 increased the infiltration of CD8+ T cells (Figure 4B and C), recapitulating our findings from the genetically engineered model.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4B and quantified in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: In the CB-1158 treatment group, GZMB was common in CD8+ T cells, while in the control tissue, GZMB expression was rare
claims.source: While in the control tissue, GZMB expression was rare, in the CB-1158 treatment group, GZMB was common in CD8+ T cells (Figure 4D and E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4D and quantified in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: A significant decrease in tumor weight was observed in the combination group of CB-1158 + anti-PD1 compared with the vehicle control group
claims.source: We observed a trending decrease in tumor weight in the CB-1158 + IgG group and a significant decrease in tumor weight in the combination group of CB-1158 + anti-PD1 immune checkpoint blockade compared with our vehicle control group (Figure 4G).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by tumor weight measurements shown in Figure 4G.

claims.claim: No changes in ARG1 distribution or expression among treatment groups were observed
claims.source: We examined ARG1 expression in macrophages (F4/80+) and epithelial (ECAD+) cells by co-immunofluorescence staining and observed no changes in ARG1 distribution or expression among treatment groups (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The CB-1158 Arginase inhibitor does not affect enzyme production but suppresses its activity
claims.source: We examined ARG1 expression in macrophages (F4/80+) and epithelial (ECAD+) cells by co-immunofluorescence staining and observed no changes in ARG1 distribution or expression among treatment groups (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), consistent with the notion that the CB-1158 Arginase inhibitor does not affect enzyme production but suppresses its activity.
claims.evidence: This represents an inference based on the observation that ARG1 protein levels don't change with CB-1158 treatment.

claims.claim: Large necrotic areas were observed in both CB-1158 and CB-1158 + anti-PD1 groups
claims.source: Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining showed large necrotic areas in both CB-1158 and CB-1158 + anti-PD1 groups (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The combination treatment group showed a significant decrease in cell proliferation compared to the vehicle control group
claims.source: The combination treatment group showed a significant decrease in cell proliferation compared to the vehicle control group (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by Ki67 staining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and quantified in 1E.

claims.claim: A significant or trending increase in CC3 was observed upon CB-1158 + IgG, vehicle + anti-PD1, or the combination treatment
claims.source: We also observed either a significant or trending increase in CC3 upon CB-1158 + IgG, vehicle + anti-PD1, or the combination treatment (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D and F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by cleaved caspase-3 staining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D and quantified in 1F.

claims.claim: An increase in arginine levels was observed in the tumors from mice treated with CB-1158 and anti-PD1
claims.source: Additionally, metabolomics analysis of these orthotopic tumors revealed an increase in arginine levels in the tumors from mice treated with CB-1158 and anti-PD1 (Figure 4H).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by metabolomics data shown in Figure 4H.

claims.claim: Arginine deprivation results in reduced CD8+ T cell proliferation and activation
claims.source: We found that arginine deprivation results in reduced CD8+ T cell proliferation and activation (Figure 4J and K).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro CD8+ T cell assay data shown in Figure 4J and K.

claims.claim: Culturing cells in RPMI media containing urea slightly enhanced CD8+ T cell proliferation and activation, compared to RPMI media control
claims.source: Additionally, we found that culturing cells in RPMI media containing urea sightly enhanced CD8+ T cell proliferation and activation, compared to RPMI media control (Figure 4J and K, gray bars)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro CD8+ T cell assay data shown in Figure 4J and K.

claims.claim: No enhancement in CD8+ T cell proliferation or activation was observed with ornithine supplementation in complete media
claims.source: Additionally, we found that culturing cells in RPMI media containing urea sightly enhanced CD8+ T cell proliferation and activation, compared to RPMI media control (Figure 4J and K, gray bars), while no enhancement was observed with ornithine supplementation.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro CD8+ T cell assay data shown in Figure 4J and K.

claims.claim: When cells were cultured in RPMI media lacking arginine, supplementation with ornithine, but not urea, partially rescued the proliferation defect caused by lack of arginine
claims.source: When cells were cultured in RPMI media lacking arginine, supplementation with ornithine, but not urea, partially rescued the proliferation defect caused by lack of arginine.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro CD8+ T cell assay data shown in Figure 4J and K.

claims.claim: Neither ornithine nor urea rescued the activation defect caused by lack of arginine
claims.source: No further rescue occurred adding urea; neither ornithine nor urea rescued the activation defect caused by lack of arginine.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro CD8+ T cell assay data shown in Figure 4J and K.

claims.claim: CD8+ T cells require arginine for proliferation and activation
claims.source: We thus concluded that CD8+ T cells require arginine for proliferation and activation, and that the arginine breakdown byproducts are not harmful to CD8+ T cell proliferation nor are they able to fully rescue lack of arginine.
claims.evidence: This represents a conclusion based on the in vitro CD8+ T cell assay data.

claims.claim: The arginine breakdown byproducts are not harmful to CD8+ T cell proliferation
claims.source: We thus concluded that CD8+ T cells require arginine for proliferation and activation, and that the arginine breakdown byproducts are not harmful to CD8+ T cell proliferation nor are they able to fully rescue lack of arginine.
claims.evidence: This represents a conclusion based on the in vitro CD8+ T cell assay data.

claims.claim: The arginine breakdown byproducts are not able to fully rescue lack of arginine for CD8+ T cell function
claims.source: We thus concluded that CD8+ T cells require arginine for proliferation and activation, and that the arginine breakdown byproducts are not harmful to CD8+ T cell proliferation nor are they able to fully rescue lack of arginine.
claims.evidence: This represents a conclusion based on the in vitro CD8+ T cell assay data.

claims.claim: Arginase inhibition in combination with anti-PD1 reduces immune suppression and decreases pancreatic cancer tumor growth
claims.source: Together, these findings indicate that Arginase inhibition in combination with anti-PD1 reduces immune suppression and decreases pancreatic cancer tumor growth (see working model in Figure 5).
claims.evidence: This represents a summary conclusion based on all the experimental data presented in the study.

claims.claim: Abundant myeloid cells in the TME are associated with poor prognosis in multiple types of cancer, including PDA

claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gentles et al., 2015; Sanford et al., 2013; and Tsujikawa et al., 2017.

claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gentles et al., 2015 and Balachandran et al., 2017.

claims.claim: Myeloid cells promote pancreatic cancer growth both directly and by inhibiting CD8+ T cell anti-tumor immunity

claims.claim: Macrophages are plastic cell types, traditionally classified into pro-inflammatory 'M1' and anti-inflammatory 'M2' subtypes, based on their gene expression pattern

claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Mantovani et al., 2002.

claims.claim: A wealth of evidence now supports the notion that TAMs are distinct from M1 and M2

claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Boyer et al., 2022; DeNardo and Ruffell, 2019; and Halbrook et al., 2019.

claims.claim: TAMs exhibit heterogeneous populations within an individual tumor
claims.source: Adding further complexity, TAMs also exhibit heterogeneous populations within an individual tumor.
claims.evidence: This represents established knowledge in the field about TAM heterogeneity.

claims.claim: ARG1 is classically considered a 'marker' of the anti-inflammatory M2 state
claims.source: ARG1 is classically considered a 'marker' of the anti-inflammatory M2 state.
claims.evidence: This represents established knowledge in the field about ARG1 as an M2 marker.

claims.claim: Arginases are enzymes that hydrolyze the amino acid L-arginine to urea and L-ornithine in the liver urea cycle
claims.source: Arginases are enzymes that hydrolyze the amino acid L-arginine to urea and L-ornithine in the liver urea cycle (Jenkinson et al., 1996).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Jenkinson et al., 1996.

claims.claim: L-arginine was drastically reduced in the tumor interstitial fluid in an autochthonous PDA mouse model

claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Sullivan et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Ornithine levels increased in the PDA tumor interstitial fluid compared to plasma
claims.source: Additionally, ornithine levels increased in the PDA tumor interstitial fluid compared to plasma (Sullivan et al., 2019), suggesting arginase contribution to immunosuppression through depletion of arginine.

results.result: ARG1 is predominantly expressed in myeloid cells in human pancreatic cancer. RNA in situ hybridization and sc-RNA-seq analysis of human PDA samples showed prevalent ARG1 expression in CD45+ immune cells (primarily myeloid cells) with minimal expression in epithelial cells, CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, and fibroblasts. ARG2 was expressed at high levels in endocrine cells and at lower levels in epithelial cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C51 are well-supported by multiple complementary techniques (RNA ISH, sc-RNA-seq) applied to human PDA samples. The data consistently show ARG1 is predominantly expressed in myeloid cells with minimal expression in other cell types. Quantification is provided in Figure 1B, and sc-RNA-seq data from 16 human samples (Figure 1D) corroborates the ISH findings.

results.result: High ARG1 expression correlates with worse survival in pancreatic cancer patients. Analysis of the GSE71729 microarray dataset showed that patients with high ARG1 expression had significantly worse overall survival compared to those with low ARG1 expression, suggesting a functional role for ARG1 in human PDA.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C54 are supported by survival analysis of a publicly available dataset (GSE71729) with 125 patients. The Kaplan-Meier analysis (Figure 1E) shows statistically significant correlation (p=0.0027) between high ARG1 expression and worse survival. However, this is correlative data and does not establish causation.

results.result: ARG1 is highly expressed in macrophages in mouse pancreatic cancer models. Sc-RNA-seq and immunofluorescence analysis showed that Arg1 expression was highest in macrophages and enriched in PDA-infiltrating macrophages compared to normal pancreas. ARG1 protein was not detected in healthy pancreas but showed frequent co-localization with F4/80+ macrophages in both PanIN and PDA lesions.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C63 are well-supported by multiple complementary approaches including sc-RNA-seq from healthy and KPC tumor-bearing mice (Figure 1G) and immunofluorescence staining (Figure 1H-I). The data consistently demonstrate macrophage-specific Arg1 expression that increases during disease progression. Quantification is provided showing significant differences between disease stages.

results.result: Genetic deletion of Arg1 in macrophages results in elevated extracellular arginine levels. Western blot confirmed efficient deletion of ARG1 protein in Lyz2Cre/+;Arg1f/f tumor-associated macrophages, and LC-MS/MS metabolomics showed elevated L-arginine in the culture medium of Arg1-deficient TAMs compared to wild-type TAMs.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C66 are supported by western blot data (Figure 2B) showing efficient Arg1 deletion and metabolomics data (Figure 2C) showing elevated arginine in Arg1-deficient TAM media. The metabolomics provides direct biochemical evidence that Arg1 deletion prevents arginine depletion. Sample sizes appear adequate (n=4 per group based on heatmap).

results.result: Myeloid-specific Arg1 deletion reduces progression to invasive pancreatic cancer but induces compensatory Arg1 expression in epithelial cells. In aged KFCA mice (9-16 months), only 21% developed invasive disease compared to 62% of control KF mice. However, KFCA mice showed substantial ARG1 expression in epithelial cells (absent in KF mice), representing a compensatory mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C73 are supported by histopathological evaluation (Figure 2E, n=24-26 per group, p<0.05 by chi-square test) and immunofluorescence data (Figure 2F). The reduced progression to invasive disease is statistically significant. The compensatory epithelial Arg1 expression is clearly demonstrated by IF staining and represents an important finding about resistance mechanisms.

results.result: Tuft cells are the source of compensatory epithelial ARG1 expression in KFCA mice. The ARG1-expressing epithelial cells in KFCA pancreata had elongated morphology consistent with tuft cells, and co-immunostaining with the tuft cell marker COX1 confirmed that tuft cells are the exclusive source of epithelial ARG1.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C77 are supported by morphological observations and co-immunostaining data (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A) showing co-localization of ARG1 with COX1+ tuft cells. The identification of tuft cells as the source is well-documented. The interpretation that this represents a response to accumulating arginine (C77) is reasonable but remains speculative.

results.result: Arg1 deletion in myeloid cells induces macrophage repolarization with reduced tumor-promoting APOE expression and compensatory Arg2 upregulation. Sc-RNA-seq identified five macrophage subpopulations with similar total macrophage percentages between KF and KFCA. KFCA macrophages showed reduced APOE expression (a tumor-promoting factor) and upregulation of Arg2, mainly in macrophage population 4.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C85 are supported by sc-RNA-seq analysis (Figure 2H-I) and immunofluorescence validation (Figure 2—figure supplement 3D-E). The identification of five macrophage subpopulations and differential gene expression patterns is well-documented. The Arg2 upregulation represents an important compensatory mechanism. However, the sc-RNA-seq is from n=1 per genotype, which limits statistical power.

results.result: KFCA macrophages show upregulation of MHC I antigen processing and presentation pathways. Reactome pathway enrichment analysis revealed that KFCA macrophages, particularly the macrophage 3 population, exhibited upregulation of signaling pathways involved in MHC I antigen processing and cross presentation, suggesting improved antigen-specific CD8+ T cell activation.
results.evaluation: Claims C86-C87 are supported by pathway enrichment analysis (Figure 2J) and differential gene expression data (Figure 2—figure supplement 3H). The upregulation of MHC I-related pathways is clearly demonstrated. However, the interpretation that this leads to improved CD8+ T cell activation (C87) is an inference that requires functional validation, which is provided in subsequent experiments.

results.result: Arg1 deletion in myeloid cells increases CD8+ T cell infiltration, activation, and exhaustion. KFCA pancreata showed increased CD8+ T cell infiltration by IHC. Sc-RNA-seq revealed increased percentages of both cytotoxic and exhausted CD8+ T cells, with upregulation of activation markers (Gzmb, Prfn1, Ifng) and exhaustion markers (Ctla4, Furin, Lag3, Pdcd1).
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C93 are well-supported by multiple complementary approaches including IHC (Figure 3A), sc-RNA-seq (Figure 3D-F, I), and immunofluorescence validation (Figure 3G-H). The data consistently show increased CD8+ T cell infiltration and activation, but also increased exhaustion markers. This represents a key finding about the dual effects of Arg1 deletion. Sample sizes appear adequate (n=5-6 for IHC, n=3 for IF).

results.result: Pharmacological arginase inhibition with CB-1158 increases CD8+ T cell infiltration and activation in orthotopic pancreatic tumors. Treatment with CB-1158 increased CD8+ T cell infiltration by IHC and increased the frequency of GZMB+ CD8+ T cells by immunofluorescence, recapitulating findings from the genetic model.
results.evaluation: Claims C94-C95 are supported by IHC data (Figure 4B-C, p=0.0325) and immunofluorescence data (Figure 4D-E). The pharmacological approach validates the genetic findings and demonstrates that systemic arginase inhibition can increase CD8+ T cell infiltration and activation. Sample sizes appear adequate (n=4-6 per group).

results.result: CB-1158 combined with anti-PD1 significantly reduces tumor growth in orthotopic pancreatic cancer. The combination treatment showed significant tumor weight reduction compared to vehicle control, with increased tumor arginine levels, large necrotic areas, decreased proliferation, and increased apoptosis. ARG1 protein expression was unchanged, consistent with CB-1158 inhibiting enzyme activity rather than expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C102 are well-supported by tumor weight measurements (Figure 4G, n=10-12 per group, p<0.05 by two-way ANOVA), metabolomics (Figure 4H), and histological analyses (Figure 4—figure supplement 1). The combination therapy shows statistically significant efficacy. The observation that ARG1 protein levels are unchanged (C97-C98) is consistent with the known mechanism of CB-1158 as an enzyme inhibitor.

results.result: CD8+ T cells require arginine for proliferation and activation, and arginine breakdown products cannot fully rescue arginine deprivation. In vitro assays showed that arginine deprivation reduced CD8+ T cell proliferation and activation. Ornithine partially rescued proliferation defects but not activation defects, while urea slightly enhanced proliferation in complete media but did not rescue arginine deprivation.
results.evaluation: Claims C103-C110 are supported by in vitro CD8+ T cell assays (Figure 4J-K) with appropriate controls and multiple conditions tested. The data clearly demonstrate arginine requirement for T cell function and show that breakdown products have limited rescue capacity. The experimental design is sound with n=3 replicates. Statistical significance is shown for key comparisons.

results.result: Arginase inhibition combined with anti-PD1 reduces immune suppression and decreases pancreatic cancer tumor growth by depleting arginine and inhibiting T cell activation. This represents the main conclusion integrating all experimental findings from genetic and pharmacological approaches.
results.evaluation: Claims C111 and C142 represent the main conclusions of the study, supported by the totality of evidence from genetic models (KFCA mice), pharmacological interventions (CB-1158), and mechanistic studies (metabolomics, T cell assays). The data consistently support the model that Arg1 drives immune suppression through arginine depletion. The combination therapy approach is well-validated.

results.result: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is characterized by poor survival, KRAS mutations, and limited treatment options. PDA is the third leading cause of cancer-related deaths with 12% 5-year survival, commonly harbors KRASG12D mutations, and current standard chemotherapy provides limited survival benefit.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C5 are background information supported by appropriate citations to established literature. These claims provide context for the study but do not represent novel findings. The citations appear appropriate and the information is consistent with current knowledge about PDA.

results.result: KRAS-targeted therapies are emerging but resistance is expected, highlighting the need for immunotherapy approaches. KRASG12C inhibitors show promise in lung cancer but have limited applicability in PDA. New KRASG12D inhibitors are entering the clinic, but resistance is expected based on lung cancer data and mouse models.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C13 are background information supported by appropriate citations. These claims provide rationale for the study's focus on immunotherapy but do not represent novel findings. The speculation about future resistance (C12-C13) is reasonable based on cited evidence but remains predictive.

results.result: The pancreatic tumor microenvironment is immunosuppressive with abundant myeloid cells and rare, exhausted CD8+ T cells. Immune checkpoint inhibitors are ineffective in PDA due to the immunosuppressive TME. Myeloid cell depletion activates anti-tumor T cell responses in mouse models, but clinical efficacy has been limited.
results.evaluation: Claims C14-C24 are background information supported by appropriate citations to established literature. These claims provide important context and rationale for the study but do not represent novel findings from this work. The citations appear appropriate and comprehensive.

results.result: ARG1 is a metabolic enzyme expressed in myeloid cells that breaks down arginine, which is necessary for CD8+ T cell function. ARG1 is expressed in tumor-associated macrophages across multiple cancer types and may deplete arginine in the TME to dampen anti-tumor T cell activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C36 are background information supported by appropriate citations, including the authors' previous work. These claims establish the biological rationale for the study. The inference that myeloid cells may deplete arginine to dampen T cell activity (C36) is reasonable based on the cited literature and is tested experimentally in this study.

results.result: CB-1158 is a small-molecule arginase inhibitor that decreased tumor growth in Lewis lung carcinoma models and is being tested in clinical trials. CB-1158 treatment as monotherapy or combined with anti-PD-1 decreased tumor growth in mice with Lewis lung carcinoma and is being tested in phase I trials in patients with solid tumors.
results.evaluation: Claims C37-C40 are background information about CB-1158 supported by appropriate citations. These claims establish the rationale for using CB-1158 in this study but do not represent novel findings. The information about clinical trials is factual and verifiable.

results.result: The study used dual-recombinase and pharmacological approaches to investigate Arg1 function in pancreatic cancer. A dual-recombinase genetic model was used to delete Arg1 in myeloid cells while inducing oncogenic Kras in epithelial cells, and a pharmacological approach using CB-1158 was employed to overcome compensatory mechanisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C44 describe the experimental approaches used in the study. These are methodological claims that are well-supported by the detailed methods section and experimental data. The dual-recombinase approach is innovative and appropriate for the research question.

results.result: Infiltration of myeloid cells, specifically macrophages, in pancreatic cancer portends worse patient survival. This is established knowledge supported by citations to Sanford et al., 2013 and Tsujikawa et al., 2017.
results.evaluation: Claim C52 is background information supported by appropriate citations. This provides context for the study but does not represent a novel finding.

results.result: Myeloid cells in the TME are associated with poor prognosis while T cells correlate with better survival. Macrophages are traditionally classified as M1/M2 but TAMs are now recognized as distinct and heterogeneous. ARG1 is classically considered an M2 marker.
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C118 are background information from the Discussion section, supported by appropriate citations. These claims provide context for interpreting the study's findings but do not represent novel results.

results.result: Arginases are enzymes that hydrolyze arginine to urea and ornithine, with two isoforms (ARG1 and ARG2) located in different cellular compartments. L-arginine is reduced in PDA tumor interstitial fluid while ornithine levels increase, suggesting arginase contribution to immunosuppression.
results.evaluation: Claims C119-C127 are background information from the Discussion section, supported by appropriate citations. The inference about arginase contribution to immunosuppression (C122) is reasonable based on the cited metabolomics data from Sullivan et al., 2019.

results.result: Prior studies in other cancer models demonstrated that myeloid Arg1 expression impairs T cell function and that arginase inhibition reduces tumor growth in a T cell-dependent manner. Studies in Lewis lung carcinoma, KrasG12D lung cancer, and neuroblastoma models showed that Arg1 expression or arginase activity promotes tumor growth.
results.evaluation: Claims C128-C132 are background information from the Discussion section, supported by appropriate citations to prior work in other cancer models. These claims provide important context showing that the concept has been validated in other systems.

results.result: CB-1158 is not cell permeable and does not inhibit liver ARG1, avoiding toxicity. In vitro, CB-1158 inhibits both human ARG1 and ARG2, and its in vivo action is attributed to inhibition of extracellular ARG1 released by myeloid cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C133-C135 are background information about CB-1158's mechanism of action, supported by citation to Steggerda et al., 2017. This information is important for understanding the drug's selectivity and mechanism.

results.result: Arg2 may play a role in obesity-driven pancreatic cancer and could be a target of CB-1158 in human patients. In obesity-driven PDA models, Arg2 is upregulated in epithelial cells and promotes tumor growth. While Arg2 was not observed in epithelial cells in non-obese KF mice, low but detectable Arg2 expression was found in human epithelial cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C136-C138 are supported by citations and data, but C139 is speculative about CB-1158's mechanism in human patients. The speculation is reasonable given the data showing Arg2 expression in human epithelial cells, but this remains untested and represents a hypothesis for future work.

results.result: Myeloid Arg1 overexpression and activity is one mechanism by which myeloid cells promote immune suppression and tumor growth in pancreatic cancer, and arginase inhibition may be an effective therapeutic strategy. This represents the authors' interpretation and therapeutic implications of their findings.
results.evaluation: Claims C140-C141 represent the authors' conclusions based on the totality of their experimental data. C140 is well-supported by the genetic and pharmacological evidence presented. C141 is more speculative about clinical translation but is reasonable based on the preclinical data and ongoing clinical trials.

results.result: CB-1158 is currently being evaluated in clinical trials as a single agent and in combination with immune checkpoint therapy or chemotherapy in patients with solid tumors. This is factual information about ongoing clinical trials.
results.evaluation: Claim C143 is factual information supported by reference to clinical trial registrations (NCT02903914 and NCT03314935). This provides important context about the clinical translation of the preclinical findings.
